Hasanbeigi, A., Price, L. and Arens, M. (2013). Emerging Energy-efficiency and Carbon Dioxide Emissions-reduction Technologies for the Iron and Steel Industry. Report LBNL-6106E, Ernest Orlando Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, CA, January 2013. No DOI or URL printed.

Locators are the report's printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 9). A review of 56 emerging technologies compiled from other sources; nearly every number is reprinted (reference named in each note); there are no per-technology summary tables, only benefit bullets and a status line. Main file (36 technologies): Section 2 conventional-process energy ranges (sinter, pellet, coke, BF, EAF, hot and cold flat rolling; Energetics 2004 / worldsteel); single-chamber coke oven capex (derived $40 million / 100,000 t/yr); the 12 alternative ironmaking processes of Sect. 3.4 (same content as hasanbeigi_2014_001: descriptions, status, cyclone converter 13-14 GJ/thm, MOE 3,500 kWh/t, PSH capex, reference-plant capacities, CO2 reduction potentials); ECOARC 196 kWh/t; primary-energy scrap melter and continuous EAF steelmaking (description/status, 70-170 t/h); Nippon strip caster 0.05 GJ/t fuel + 42 kWh/t, 420 kt/yr; PRIMUS 1,100 kWh/t dust; Pickliq 0.92 kWh/kg dissolved iron; TGR-BF (-35%), ULCORED, HIsarna (-20%) and HIsarna+CCS (-80%), MDEA regeneration 3.2 GJ/t CO2, BF-gas amine capture (<50%) and shift+amine (85-99.5%). _measures.csv: every other technology (retrofit/add-on measures, controls, sensors, injection and recycling practices) with the saving, cost and payback where printed, and the relative savings of the whole technologies. _other-values.csv: pilot capacities, alternative operating points, temperatures, whole-route CO2 figures and targets. Not loaded: Table 2 qualitative matrix, qualitative bullets. Digits missing from the PDF text layer on p.63-64 were read from the rendered page. No flows file (no per-unit input quantities besides oxygen in Nm3, kept in notes).

(1) Compiled values from company claims and older studies, not original results. (2) No currency or price year for any cost (SCS $40 million, PSH $16,729,000, hot oxygen $1.05 million, recuperation $18-20/GJ, scale-free reheating $0.75-2.8 million, Voestalpine EUR 20 million) and no cost basis. (3) PDF text layer drops some digits (p.63-64: '2000', '40,000', '2002', 'EUR 20 million'). (4) Table 1 section numbers disagree with the text (e.g. 3.4.7 for carbon composite agglomerates, 3.9.10-3.9.12 for plastics/tires, 3.6.4 for continuous EAF, 3.6.2 for HotEye); Sect. 3.4.9 cross-references a non-existent 3.10.3 for HIsarna. (5) Sect. 3.4.2 (FINEX) introduces its benefits as 'reported for COREX'. (6) Typos: '9,00 degC' (MXCOL), '15,00 degC' (arc temperature), 'Nm3 = cubic nanometer' in the acronym list. (7) Energy figures give no heating-value basis or carrier split; Section 2 ranges are totals. (8) Emission-reduction percentages use different baselines (per t product, benchmark steel mill, BF route). (9) SCS '38- to 70-percent more thermally efficient' has no stated basis. (10) Strip caster fuel type not stated.
